fields.System.Title: EPIC INV — Inventory Core
fields.System.Description:
Goal

Know how much of what is where, in what status — and be able to explain every number from an
immutable record of movements.

Business value

This is the epic the whole system rests on. Every other epic is a way of asking inventory to
change something. If these numbers cannot be trusted, nothing built on top of them can be.

The promise this epic makes is narrow and absolute:

> Every balance change wrote a movement. Balances can always be rebuilt from the ledger.

Scope

In. Stock balances by product, location, batch and status. The append-only movement ledger.
Moving stock. Status changes. Reservations. Batches and expiry. Adjustments with reason codes
and approval. Reconciliation. The availability projection.

Out. Deciding why stock should move. Receiving decides that. Allocation decides that.
Inventory only executes and records.

Done when

  • Stock can be queried by location, by product, and by batch.
  • Every balance change has a matching movement row, verified by a reconciliation job.
  • Two concurrent moves against the same balance produce a correct result.
  • On-hand can never go negative and reserved can never exceed on-hand.
  • Reservations can be created, released, and consumed, and never leak.
  • An adjustment requires a reason code and, above a threshold, an approval.
  • The availability projection reconciles nightly against the balances.

Key risks

| Risk | Why it matters | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Lost update on concurrent change | Stock silently wrong; the classic WMS bug | [doc 09 §4.1](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Balance written without a movement | The ledger stops explaining reality | [doc 09 §2.2](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| On-hand and reserved diverge | Negative availability; orders fail against present stock | [doc 09 §2.3](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Reservation leaks | Stock invisible forever | [doc 09 §5.2](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Deadlock on multi-location operations | Random failures at peak | [doc 09 §4.2](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Allocating from the projection | The same unit sold twice | [doc 09 §12](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
